# Cross-Repo & CI Ordering Checklist: Comprehensive live QuickFIX interop conversation

**Purpose**: Requirements-quality review of the clauses spanning the two repositories — digest pinning, republish ordering, consumer blast radius, and the capability handshake (FR-016a/b/c, FR-026, R-11).
**Created**: 2026-09-10
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md) · [research.md](../research.md) §R-11 · [plan.md](../plan.md) §External obligations

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

> ⚠️ **This domain produced two defects that survived ten Gate A rounds**, both of the same shape: an
> obligation stated in one artifact and unreachable from the artifact a reader would consult. R-11
> decided *"pin `interop-smoke.yml` **and the existing cells**"*; the obligations table recorded only the
> first half, and the file carrying the second half had no row at all. These items test for more of it.

## Failure Direction of the Consumers

- [x] CHK013 Are requirements defined for the case where the image cannot be pulled — specifically that the consumer **skips with a reason and stays GREEN** — so that "089 is passing" is not read as "the cell ran"? [Coverage, Gap] — PASS: `spec.md`:367-369 (*"A skip must never satisfy a fidelity assertion, and the new evidence rows must record a skip as a skip"*) and FR-016 (838-839, *"A counterparty-unavailable outcome MUST remain distinguishable from a pass in both the cell result and the evidence record"*) state this directly. Non-PASS: no requirement distinguishing skip from pass, leaving "089 is passing" ambiguous with "the cell ran."
- [x] CHK014 Is the rule that an **unpullable pin is a skip, and a skip is green** stated at every site that pins a digest? [Consistency, Gap] — SPEC-FIXED: ⚠️ **RE-VERIFIED AND RESTORED 2026-09-10.** This disposition asserted the rule was carried at **both** consumer obligation rows. That was true when written and **FALSE from `69a5112c` until now**: emptying the pin obligations deleted the failure-direction language from both rows, and neither the FR-026 rewrite nor the first confirmation pass noticed. Both rows now carry it again — ⛔ **re-keyed off pinning**, because the hazard never depended on it: under FR-026 the consumers resolve the mutable `:latest`, so an unpullable image still skips them to green. ⚠️ **Scope seam, stated not silently closed**: FR-016b's MUST reads *"every site that pins a digest"* and neither consumer pins any more, so for them the obligation lives in the `plan.md` rows rather than in FR-016b. Original evidence follows. FR-016b now reads *"AN UNPULLABLE PIN IS A SKIP, AND A SKIP IS GREEN"* with the anti-vacuity question spelled out — *ask what ELSE satisfies "the pinned cell passed": the cell not having run* — and each row repeats the failure direction for its own workflow rather than pointing away from itself.
- [x] CHK015 Are requirements specified for evidencing that a cell **actually ran**, as distinct from the job reporting success? [Measurability, Gap] — SPEC-FIXED: ⚠️ **RE-VERIFIED AND RESTORED 2026-09-10 — see CHK014: the *"both rows carry it"* claim was falsified by `69a5112c` and is true again only after the restore.** The *actually-ran* obligation is lifted out of `tasks.md` T104 and stated normatively for the pre-existing consumer cells this domain concerns: *"every site that pins a digest MUST also evidence that the cell **actually executed**, read from that run's own **step log** and never from the job conclusion."* Each of the two rows carries it for its own workflow. This does not extend FR-014's Level-1 population to those cells — it states the weaker, correct obligation for them, which is that a green check is not evidence the cell ran.
- [x] CHK016 Is a counterparty-unavailable outcome required to remain distinguishable from a pass in **both** the cell result and the evidence record? [Completeness, Spec §FR-016] — PASS: `spec.md` FR-016 (838-839) is a verbatim match. Non-PASS: the requirement silent on one of the two locations (cell result or evidence record).

## Ambiguities & Conflicts

- [x] CHK026 Does any requirement in this domain state a pinned digest, tag or version as a **value** where the value will move, without a re-derivation recipe? [Clarity, Gap] — PASS: no literal digest/SHA/version value that will move is written anywhere in the bundle (checked: no `sha256:` literal, no hard-coded "current" digest for "the pre-089 digest"); the capability-minimums row and `spec.md` FR-023a both explicitly decline to write a value that would rot, in favour of a re-derivation recipe or a value deferred to implementation time. Non-PASS: a literal `sha256:...` or version string written as "the pre-089 digest" with no recipe to re-derive it once it moves.
- [x] CHK027 Are `FR-020`'s regression obligation and the republish safety argument distinguished — i.e. is it clear that reasoning about an opt-in gate is not the measurement FR-020 requires? [Conflict, Spec §FR-020] — SPEC-FIXED: **applied at `spec.md`:911 (FR-020 itself)** — *"THIS IS A MEASUREMENT — RUN THE CELLS AND COMPARE — AND AN ARGUMENT IS NOT ONE"*, naming the specific substitution the item describes (arguing safety from the counterparty emitter activating only when `INTEROP_CP_RUN_ID` is set) and why it cannot discharge the clause: it reasons about a mechanism and runs **zero** existing cells. ⚠️ **The measurement is given a producer in the same clause** — `tasks.md` T099 — so the new MUST does not itself become an obligation with nothing behind it, which is the RC-A shape this bundle just closed twice elsewhere in this batch.
- [x] CHK028 Do the requirements name which repository each obligation lands in, at every row, so a reader never has to infer it from a path prefix? [Clarity] — PASS: `plan.md` § *Project Structure* (447, 462) names the two repositories once, with explicit `# ── PARENT repo:` / `# ── LIBRARY submodule:` headers, and every row in § *External obligations* follows that path-prefix convention consistently (`library/...` vs `phase-9-harness/...`) with no row breaking it. Non-PASS: rows mixing prefixes inconsistently, or the convention never declared, forcing a reader to infer the partition from context alone.

outright**. R-11 then said *"**Decision**: pin … Recorded as **FR-026**"* while FR-026 mandated the
opposite, and its consolidated-impact row asserted as present fact that *"the `:latest` blast radius is
closed by pinning existing consumers to the pre-089 digest first (FR-026)"* — **an active false
attribution, not an unmarked historical record.** ⭐ **That distinction is the whole of it**: leaving a
superseded prescription unmarked is a stale record; leaving a claim that attributes to a live requirement
the opposite of what it says is a defect. R-11 now carries a supersede marker at its heading and its
struck Decision, and its consolidated-impact row has been rewritten. Its dated reasoning is preserved
struck-through; only the prescription is dead.
